---
title: "check-result-definition-links.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check for the lab's rule
(Ezra, 2026-11-09)
that every result div links at least one definition.
A reader of a theorem, lemma, corollary, or proposition
can then reach the meaning of the terms it uses.

The check flags a `#thm-`, `#lem-`, `#cor-`, or `#prp-` div
that holds no definition link.
A definition link is either:

- a cross-reference to a definition, such as `@def-id`; or
- a Markdown link whose target ends in `#def-id`,
  on this site or on a prerequisite site.

A link inside a comment or a code fence does not count.
A link in a nested proof does count.
A result with no defined term to link,
such as an identity between numbers,
is exempt with `<!-- check-result-definition-links: allow: reason -->`.

A div is checked when the pull request adds a line inside it.
With no base to diff against,
the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree,
so existing results are fixed when someone edits them anyway.
It only warns by default;
set `fail: true` after a measured corpus shows no false positive.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive) |
| `paths-ignore` | none | Comma or newline separated globs to skip |
| `fail` | `false` | Fail on a finding; `false` warns |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Check every result div, to measure a corpus |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version |
| `runs-on` | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label; a self-hosted label only for a private repository |

## Usage

Copy `examples/check-result-definition-links.yml` to
`.github/workflows/check-result-definition-links.yml`.
